moves_attempted: generalize the index-two character grading to higher finite character quotients
extract a stable noisy reconstruction statement
compile the proof into a direct reconstruction algorithm
translate the result into finite phase-retrieval sufficiency language
route_delta: The singleton-character proof is simultaneously a rigidity theorem, a linear-time decoder in the parity case, and a sharp warning that the Laurent-domain step is the only place torsion-freeness enters.  Its Z/2 grading may be the first member of a higher finite-grading reconstruction theory, but the quadratic sum/product collapse is special and must not be assumed for larger quotients.

seeds.title: Higher-character anchor rigidity
seeds.exact_seed: Let Gamma be torsion-free abelian and chi:Gamma→mu_k a finite character.  Determine the minimal graded-fiber profile, stronger than one singleton fiber alone when k>2, for which labeled autocorrelation determines a finite subset up to translation and inversion.
seeds.evidence: For k=2, the even/odd decomposition reduces equality of autocorrelations to equal sums and products of two group-ring elements.  The same grading produces a finite cyclic system for k>2 but no two-factor collapse is yet proved.
seeds.cheap_test: Exhaust subsets of small boxes in Z and Z^2 for k=3,4,5, grouped by fiber profile, and find the smallest profile that has no nontrivial homometric pair before attempting group-ring elimination.
seeds.kill_condition: A small torsion-free counterexample with the proposed profile shows the Z/2 theorem is exceptional rather than the first general case.

seeds.title: Stable character-anchor recovery
seeds.exact_seed: For finite subsets in a bounded torsion-free window with one character fiber of size one, lower-bound the distance between labeled autocorrelations of two non-equivalent sets in terms of the coefficient norm and window diameter, and construct a decoder tolerating errors below half that separation.
seeds.evidence: Exact rigidity makes the finite channel injective; integrality gives unit separation in unweighted coefficient norms, while noisy weighted/normalized versions require a nontrivial stability analysis.
seeds.cheap_test: Enumerate all anchored sets through moderate diameter, compute the minimum l1/l2 autocorrelation separation after symmetry quotient, and test whether the exact unit bound or a sharper size-dependent formula is attained.
seeds.kill_condition: The normalized separation decays faster than any useful bound or the proposed metric is not invariant under the allowed symmetries.

seeds.title: Parity-anchor decoder
seeds.exact_seed: Given the labeled positive-difference multiplicities of an integer set whose parity classes have sizes 1 and N-1, reconstruct the normalized set in one scan of the odd lags, with only the global reflection ambiguity.
seeds.evidence: After translating the singleton parity point to zero, each positive odd lag occurs exactly when the corresponding opposite-parity point is present; the hostile audit checked the endpoint/reflection cases.
seeds.cheap_test: Implement the decoder and exhaustively compare it with all homometric classes through diameter 20, emitting explicit failure witnesses for malformed input.
seeds.kill_condition: Labeled group differences are replaced by norms, unlabeled bags, or quotient-valued differences; those observations do not support the decoder.

seeds.title: Torsion obstruction atlas
seeds.exact_seed: Classify the smallest finite abelian groups and character-fiber profiles admitting nontrivial singleton-character homometric pairs, beginning with the audited Z/12 witness.
seeds.evidence: The proof uses that a finitely generated torsion-free group ring is a Laurent-polynomial domain.  In Z/12 the independently audited sets {0,1,4,6} and {0,1,3,7} have identical autocorrelation and singleton parity fibers without translation/inversion equivalence.
seeds.cheap_test: Exhaust finite abelian groups of order at most 64 and record minimal witnesses by invariant-factor type and character kernel.
seeds.kill_condition: The census shows no structural pattern beyond isolated zero-divisor accidents, leaving a data atlas but no theorem seed.

conclusion: The most valuable next result is the higher-character profile classification, with the stable decoder as the most direct CPU theorem.  The torsion witness confirms that the current theorem's domain hypothesis is structural rather than cosmetic.
